subject: Checkout latency & throughput: recommendation and pilot next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@brightretail.com>
Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex@fastcheckout.io>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout latency & throughput: recommendation and pilot next steps

Hi Sarah — great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to align on Hosted vs Dedicated: 

Summary of requirements (from call):
- Peak concurrent inference: ~250 qps sustained during promo spikes (10–15 min windows).
- P95 latency target: <= 120ms for token-generation on the checkout personalization endpoint (avg prompt length ~120 tokens).
- Throughput sensitivity: bursty traffic, but baseline steady-state is ~40–60 qps.
- Data controls: some PII in session payloads; they want encrypted in transit + optional VPC for log retention.

Redwood recommendation (initial):
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is the safer fit for the peak+SLA profile. It gives predictable per-token latency and predictable tail latency during the 250 qps spikes.
- Hosted API could work for early validation but would require daytime throttles or higher-cost autoscaling for the promo windows; less predictable tail latency guarantees.
- Private VPC/on-prem is optional at a later stage if compliance requires complete network isolation — not required for initial pilot.

Attachments I’m including from our side: call recording + the latency samples you shared so we can baseline kernels and batching.

Proposed next steps:
1) If you're comfortable, we run a short capacity-sizing spike test (1–2 hours) on Dedicated to validate P95 and cost profile.
2) Redwood provides a scoped pilot quote + SLA draft for Dedicated (see attached estimate).
3) Schedule a technical workshop with your infra/ops (we can include our SRE) to confirm VPC/KMS needs.

Can you confirm the promo windows (UTC times) and whether the 250 qps is a sustained concurrent rate or short bursts aggregated across shards? Also confirming Alex is your engineering lead — looping him for the technical workshop.

Thanks — I’ll stand up a short Dedicated estimate and a pilot plan once you confirm.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0214

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@brightretail.com>

Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex@fastcheckout.io>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout latency & throughput: recommendation and pilot next steps

Thanks Jordan — good summary. Quick clarifications so we can make a call on procurement: 

- The 250 qps number is peak sustained for ~10 minutes during promotional pushes; outside those windows we see ~45 qps.
- Our target is P95 for the end-to-end call (inc. network + inference) < 150ms. If Redwood can guarantee inference P95 < 120ms we should be able to meet end-to-end with our infra tweaks.
- Important: we prefer not to manage GPUs; dedicated reserved capacity with an SLA is better for our team.

Two asks before we sign off on a pilot: 
1) Can you provide a ballpark committed monthly price for the Dedicated pool size that would cover those promo peaks? Useful for budgeting with procurement.
2) What does the pilot look like operationally? We’d like a short smoke test that replays our traffic to validate tail latency.

Looping Alex for infra confirmation on the replay/test approach.

—Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Product, BrightRetail
sarah.lin@brightretail.com

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout latency & throughput: recommendation and pilot next steps (internal)

Jordan — quick internal note after scanning their latency samples and the traffic profile Sarah sent.

- If we size a Dedicated pool with 4 x A100-equivalent nodes (config for continuous KV cache + batching), we should hit P95 inference latency ~90–110ms at 250 qps with optimized batching and reduced kernel warmup. The attached estimate shows committed monthly pricing and a short 2-hour spike test plan.
- Pilot plan: 1) replay their captured traffic in our staging on Dedicated (2 hours, including a warmup); 2) run a 3x promo-level spike to validate tail; 3) capture detailed token-level traces and cost-per-token.
- Risks: if their payloads include large context (>>120 tokens) or multimodal ops we'll need to re-evaluate GPU memory footprint.

I attached the draft estimate (RDW_dedicated_estimate.pdf). Recommend we present this as the default pilot + an optional Hosted fallback for initial smoke if they want to avoid procurement lead times.

cc: Marissa for CSM handoff and onboarding coordination.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@brightretail.com>
Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex@fastcheckout.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout latency & throughput: recommendation and pilot next steps

Thanks Sarah — appreciate the clarity. Based on Avery’s sizing and your constraints, here’s a practical path forward: 

Proposed commitment (pilot + optional extension):
- Pilot: 2-week pilot on a small Dedicated pool (4 A100-eq nodes) with a scoped 2-hour replay + one promo spike test. We will guarantee inference P95 <= 120ms during the validated test window.
- Ballpark committed monthly price (post-pilot, reserved): $42k/month for the pool (includes SRE-managed operations, basic observability, and token-level traces). Exact number will be formalized in the quote — this is a budgetary figure for procurement.
- If procurement/budget delays, we can run an initial 72-hour Hosted validation to gather additional traces but without SLA guarantees.

Operational checklist for pilot:
- We need: replay logs (already provided), exact promo window timestamps (local timezone), and an infra contact for network routing (Alex).
- Redwood will provide: pilot runbook, on-call SRE for the test window, and a short SLA draft (attached).

Next actions:
1) Sarah confirm the promo windows in UTC and the procurement lead time.
2) If OK, I’ll send a formal pilot Statement of Work + DocuSign link and schedule the workshop with Alex/Marissa/Avery.

DocuSign pilot SOW link: https://docusign.com/s/rdw/BR-4721 (placeholder)
Pilot SOW + SLA draft attached: deployment_summary.pdf, SLA_draft.docx

Looking forward — will keep the pilot scoped to cost + latency validation.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
